snapshot.title: SSC Full Syllabus Simulation — Tier 1 Level
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC Victory Hook: Speed simulation. 60 mins. 4 sections. No ego. Move fast. Accuracy matters.

quick_notes.title: Tier 1 Strategy
quick_notes.detail: 1. Reasoning (12-15 mins). 2. GK (5-7 mins). 3. English (10-12 mins). 4. Math (25-30 mins). Total 60 mins.
quick_notes.explanation: SSC stands for Staff Selection Commission, which conducts exams for government jobs in India. Tier 1 is the first stage of the SSC Combined Graduate Level (CGL) exam, consisting of four sections tested in a single 60-minute paper. The strategy is to spend 12 to 15 minutes on the Reasoning section, 5 to 7 minutes on General Knowledge (GK), 10 to 12 minutes on English, and 25 to 30 minutes on Mathematics, using the full hour. This time plan helps you attempt all sections without running out of time.

quick_notes.title: Target Score
quick_notes.detail: Aim for 150+ in this mock. Accuracy must be >90% in English and Reasoning.
quick_notes.explanation: In this practice test, called a mock exam, your goal is to score 150 or more total points. The test has different sections, including English and Reasoning, and you must answer at least 90 out of every 100 questions correctly in each of those two sections, which is an accuracy of over 90 percent. This means you should focus on getting most English and Reasoning questions right rather than just answering many questions quickly.

quick_notes.title: Section Mix
quick_notes.detail: Includes: Analogy, Number System, Voice, Narration, Ancient History, Rivers, and Percentage.
quick_notes.explanation: This lesson covers several different topics. An analogy is a comparison showing how two things are similar, often used in reasoning questions to find the relationship between pairs of words. The number system includes different types of numbers like natural numbers (counting numbers 1, 2, 3) and whole numbers (0 plus natural numbers). In English grammar, voice shows whether the subject acts (active voice, as in "The boy kicked the ball") or is acted upon (passive voice, as in "The ball was kicked by the boy"), while narration refers to reporting someone's words either directly (exact words in quotes) or indirectly (paraphrased without quotes). Ancient history covers human civilizations before the Middle Ages, such as the Indus Valley Civilization. Rivers are natural flowing water bodies, and in geography they are studied for their sources, courses, and uses. A percentage is a way to express a number as a fraction of 100, often written with a percent sign, like 25% meaning 25 out of 100.

quick_notes.title: Elimination Method
quick_notes.detail: If you can eliminate two options, take a calculated risk.
quick_notes.explanation: TITLE: Elimination Method The Elimination Method is a test-taking strategy used when you do not know the correct answer to a multiple-choice question. First, carefully read the question and each answer choice, then cross out any options you are certain are wrong. If you can confidently eliminate two of the four answer choices, you have narrowed the field to just two remaining options, which gives you a 50% chance of guessing correctly. At this point, it is often a smart calculated risk to make your best guess from the remaining two choices, because leaving the question blank guarantees a zero, while guessing gives you a real chance to get the point. Remember, you should only eliminate an option if you have a clear reason it is wrong, such as a fact that directly contradicts it.

quick_notes.title: Time Management
quick_notes.detail: If a math question takes >1 min, SKIP and move on.
quick_notes.explanation: TITLE: Time Management In an exam, if a math question takes more than one minute to solve, you should skip it and move on to the next question. This means you do not waste time struggling with one hard problem when you could be answering easier questions that you know. After you finish all the questions you can do quickly, you can come back to the skipped ones if you have time left. The goal is to get as many correct answers as possible in the total time given, not to finish every single problem in order.
